conceptZh: 玩具豬探長調查一碗米飯，放大鏡卻把鼻頭黏住的米粒照得巨大；線索揭曉後，飯碗下降，露出清楚的「米」。
object: A toy rice bowl, one sticky rice grain, and a cartoon pig detective with a magnifying glass.
morph: Use a mechanical reveal: the rice bowl lowers into the stage, uncovering a complete, rigid six-stroke 米 plaque without rearranging grains or deforming strokes.
creativeAngle: 豬探長認真找線索，卻被自己鼻頭上放大的米粒嚇得帽子輕輕跳起；改用飯碗下降揭字，避免把「米」誤做成十字加四點。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated toy-theater clip with warm pastel lighting and a light cream background. A stylized cartoon pig detective wears a tiny felt detective hat and investigates a centered toy bowl of cooked rice. Use one coherent detective theme, rounded toy materials, and a fixed frontal camera with generous margins.

From 0.0–1.8 seconds, the pig leans in from beside the bowl and carefully sweeps a magnifying glass over the rice. One sticky rice grain attaches to his snout. He pauses solemnly, unaware of it. From 1.8–3.2 seconds, he brings the lens toward his snout: the attached grain suddenly looks enormous through the glass. His eyes widen and his hat gives one small springy hop. He lowers the lens, revealing the tiny grain still stuck there—the entire comic payoff. Keep the reaction gentle and silent.

From 3.2–4.3 seconds, the pig backs out sideways while the rice bowl smoothly descends into the stage, revealing a complete, flat, saturated vermilion Traditional Chinese glyph 米 standing centered behind it. The reveal preserves a correctly formed six-stroke glyph: two separate upper diagonal strokes, a horizontal stroke, a central vertical stroke, and the lower left-falling and right-falling strokes. Use a clear standard printed form, with no grain textures or decorative stroke substitutions. By 4.3 seconds all props and the pig have cleared the frame. Hold only 米 perfectly still and unobstructed through 8.0 seconds, filling approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The ONLY spoken line is exactly "米、米、米飯". Say the first 米 around 0.7 seconds, the second around 2.1 seconds, and 米飯 around 5.2 seconds while the finished glyph is fully visible. Allow natural pauses. Silent pronunciation directions, never spoken or displayed: 米 = ㄇㄧˇ = mǐ; 米飯 = mǐ fàn. Use the same mǐ reading for all three occurrences. Stop after 米飯. No other dialogue or music. Display only the single target glyph 米; no vocabulary text, subtitles, pronunciation labels, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
direction:
孩子偏好：機器人、蝙蝠俠、搞笑、足球、戰鬥機器人、豬探長、樂高積木、漫威。This clip should use ONE coherent theme, not a crowded crossover. Theme: Pig Detective 豬探長 as a cartoon pig in a detective hat investigates a rice bowl; one sticky rice grain on his snout is the silly clue. Use clearly stylized toys or cartoon animals; costume characters must be obviously toy/robot figures. Keep the character itself and its meaning central; the prop gag is brief and the final glyph remains correct, unobstructed, large and still for at least 3 seconds. No logos or written character names on screen.
PRONUNCIATION LOCK: target 米, Bopomofo ㄇㄧˇ, Mandarin pinyin mǐ. The ONLY spoken line must be exactly "米、米、米飯". Example word is fixed as 米飯, pronounced mǐ fàn. Do not substitute a word. Both isolated readings and the target syllable inside the word must have exactly the same reading. Include this exact spoken line and these pronunciation guides explicitly in promptEn, stating that Bopomofo/pinyin are silent pronunciation directions, never spoken or displayed. Use clear Taiwanese Mandarin, no extra dialogue, no character catchphrases. Avoid other polyphonic examples or reading alternatives anywhere in the narration instructions. Themes affect the visual gag only, never the spoken vocabulary.

conceptZh: 積木小隊合力舉起一粒大米，卻被壓成滑稽的扁堆；大家重新分工，排成清楚的「米」。
object: An earnest squad of six expressive interlocking brick beams and one oversized uncooked rice grain
morph: After their rice-lifting tower collapses, the six brick beams deliberately slide and rotate into the six correctly proportioned strokes of 米, then their surface details recede into a clean solid glyph.
creativeAngle: 把小小米粒變成積木小隊搬不動的大貨物，以逞強疊高、整隊壓扁的反差製造笑點。倒下後由六根積木各自負責一筆，明確保留上方兩個短斜筆與下方兩個長撇捺，避免排成四點或星形。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized animation featuring an original squad of six interlocking building-brick beams with tiny expressive faces and retractable cartoon feet. They are enthusiastic, overly confident team players. Their sole supporting object is one oversized ivory uncooked rice grain, visibly elongated with a delicate lengthwise groove. Use a pale butter-yellow background, saturated vermilion bricks, soft toy-like lighting, and a locked frontal camera. Keep the teaching action centered and entirely inside generous frame margins.

At 0.0–1.5 seconds, the squad marches into a compact stack beneath the rice grain, proudly raising it overhead. Their differing beam lengths will later become the six strokes of 米. The top beam gives a smug little eyebrow lift while the bottom beam's feet begin to wobble. At 1.5–2.2 seconds, hold a brief, readable anticipation: every face looks down toward those wobbling feet. At 2.2–3.0 seconds, the tower concertinas into a comically flat stack, with six surprised faces peeking out in a vertical row. The rice grain settles gently on top like an enormous cushion, then rolls off the stack and exits the frame. Use a soft plastic clatter and a tiny squeak, never a startling crash.

At 3.0–4.6 seconds, the determined squad recovers through coordinated movement: the long vertical beam rises upright, the horizontal beam slides across its middle, two short beams rotate into the separate upper diagonal strokes, and two longer beams extend into the lower left-falling and right-falling strokes. Animate these as deliberate sliding and pivoting movements, with no explosive burst or instantaneous snapping. Follow the exact geometry of a standard Traditional Chinese printed 米: two separate inward-sloping upper strokes above the horizontal, a central horizontal and vertical cross, and the long lower spreading 撇 and 捺. Preserve the characteristic spacing, junctions, and tapered stroke ends; do not make a symmetrical asterisk or four dots around a cross.

By 4.6 seconds, their faces, feet, studs, and seams have smoothly receded, leaving one clean, flat, solid vermilion 米. Hold this correctly formed glyph completely still and unobstructed from 4.6 through 8.0 seconds, centered at approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. The rice grain and all separate objects are now out of view.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The exact and only spoken line is "米、米、米飯". Pronounce the first 米 at approximately 0.5 seconds, the second 米 at 2.0 seconds, and 米飯 at 5.3 seconds during the clear final hold. Use ㄇㄧˇ for 米 throughout, with natural pauses and an unhurried delivery. Stop after 米飯. Keep sound effects soft beneath the voice; no music. The only on-screen text is the single target glyph 米, with no subtitles, vocabulary text, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
